query: For additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components, what single intervention could improve dimensional precision and mechanical integrity while reducing fabrication-induced defects? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the current fabrication baseline, defines the processing and application conditions under which it should hold, identifies supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Substrate preheating during the additive manufacturing of high-entropy alloys will reduce thermal gradients, resulting in lower residual stress and fewer fabrication-induced defects, thereby improving both dimensional precision and mechanical integrity of the final parts.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloy powder processed using conventional laser-based additive manufacturing at ambient substrate temperature, exhibiting notable residual stress, microstructural defects (e.g., porosity, micro-cracks), and dimensional inaccuracies.
generation.intervention: Preheat the build substrate to an optimized temperature range during the laser powder-bed fusion process.
generation.conditions: Maintain identical processing parameters (laser power, scan strategy, atmosphere, etc.) for both preheated and non-preheated (ambient) builds; conduct builds in a controlled inert-gas environment; applicable on standard high-entropy alloy compositions under typical laboratory conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: Reduced thermal gradients and slower cooling rates at the melt pool boundaries induced by preheating lead to decreased residual stress and a more uniform microstructure.
generation.mechanism: Elevating the substrate temperature minimizes the temperature differential between the melting pool and the baseplate, leading to a slower, more controlled solidification process. This reduction in thermal shock helps lessen the formation of residual stresses and suppresses defect generation (such as micro-cracking and porosity), which in turn refines dimensional precision and augments mechanical properties.
generation.predicted_outcome: Components produced with preheated substrates will demonstrate higher dimensional accuracy, improved mechanical properties (e.g., enhanced tensile strength and hardness), and a lower density of fabrication-induced defects compared to those produced at ambient substrate temperature.
generation.baseline: Additively manufactured high-entropy alloy components produced with a non-preheated (ambient) substrate.
generation.boundary: Improvements are anticipated under conventional laser powder-bed fusion settings within standard high-entropy alloy compositions. The exact optimal preheat temperature and its scalability across different alloy systems or extreme build geometries remain uncertain.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal preheat temperature and its precise quantitative effects on mechanical properties and defect reduction are not yet fully established; additional parametric studies may be needed to refine these values.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate two sets of high-entropy alloy components using identical laser powder-bed fusion parameters, differing only in the substrate temperature: one set with optimized substrate preheating and one set at ambient temperature. Perform dimensional measurements, microstructural analyses (via micro-CT or SEM for defect evaluation), and mechanical testing (tensile strength, hardness) on both sample sets.
measurements: Component dimensional accuracy (e.g., using coordinate measuring machine)
Defect density and microstructural uniformity (via micro-CT scanning and SEM)
Mechanical properties: tensile strength and hardness
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the preheated samples do not exhibit a statistically significant improvement (e.g., p-value < 0.05) in dimensional precision, mechanical performance, and a reduction in defect density compared to the ambient samples, then the hypothesis is falsified.
